AN ACT to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to designating human
organ delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4071

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to designating
human organ delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles

 
PURPOSE:

To designate human organ delivery vehicles and their operations as that
of an authorized emergency vehicle.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends section 101 of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to desig-
nate and authorize human organ delivery vehicles as emergency vehicles.

Section 2: Amends section 114-b of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to add
transporting human organs or tissue, or medical personnel for the
purpose of organ recovery or transplantation in a situation involving an
imminent health risk to the definition of emergency operation.

Section 3: Adds a new section 117-e to the Vehicle and Traffic Law to
define human organ delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles,
and to require that drivers of said vehicles have had appropriate train-
ing in regards to operating an emergency vehicle. It also requires that
any such vehicle is operated by or on behalf of an organ procurement
organization, as defined in the Public Health Law.

Section 4: Sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Organ transplants and the transport of organs are a time sensitive proc-
esses. New York State should expand the designation of authorized emer-
gency vehicles to include vehicles that are carrying organs for trans-
plantation. This change will better serve the citizens of the State who
are in need of medical service. By allowing these vehicles to flash
lights, they are designating the transport of organs and organ related
paraphernalia as an emergency allowing the vehicles to navigate through
traffic better, saving money and more importantly lives. Passing this
legislation will bring New York in line with other states, including
Pennsylvania and New Jersey.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: COMMITTED TO RULES

 
FISCAL IMPLICATION:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE IT:,

This act shall take effect immediately.

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4071A

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the vehicle and traffic law, in relation to designating
human organ delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To define human organ delivery vehicles and their operation and to
designate them as an authorized emergency vehicle.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1: Amends section 101 of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to add
human organ delivery vehicles to the list of authorized emergency vehi-
cles. -

Section 2: Amends section 114-b of the Vehicle and Traffic Law to amend
the definition of "emergency operation" to include the transporting of
human organs and/or medical personnel for the purpose of organ recovery
or transplantation in a situation involving an imminent health risk
where undue delay would jeopardize such recovery or transplantation.

Section 3: Adds a new section 117-e to the Vehicle and Traffic Law to
define human organ delivery vehicles and to establish requirements and
standards for their operation. Certified organ procurement organizations
that own and operate such vehicles must be in compliance with Article
43-b of the Public Health Law. Human organ delivery vehicles must be
used solely for the purpose of transporting human organs and/or medical
personnel for the purpose of organ recovery or transplantation while
engaged,in an emergency operation, be designated and clearly identified
as a human organ delivery vehicle and have been authorized in writing to
operate as such by the Commissioner of Health, and be in compliance with
the Vehicle and Traffic Law and with regulations to be promulgated by
the Commissioner of Health for standards of operation. The bill requires
drivers of such vehicles to have undergone training approved by the
Department of Health for the operation of authorized emergency vehicles
during emergency operations, as well as to have taken a defensive driv-
ing course. The Commissioner of Health is authorized to suspend or
revoke the written authorization on proof that an organ procurement
organization failed to comply with the requirements or standards,
subject to due process and enforcement provisions under the Public
Health Law.

This new section also directs the Commissioner of Health, in consulta-
tion with the Commissioner of Motor Vehicles, to promulgate rules and
regulations establishing standards for the operation of human organ
delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles.

Section 4: Sets the effective date.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

The amendments clarify requirements and standards for the operation of
human organ delivery vehicles, and change the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:
Time is of the essence when transporting organs for emergencies, and
ambulance services are not necessarily always available in time when
needed. Under current New York State law, the options for transporting
organs are too narrow, and need to be expanded so that more vehicles can
serve this critical role. Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, and Illinois define
organ transplant vehicles and include them in their list of authorized
emergency vehicles. When lives are on the line and every second matters,
it is important that New York State does everything we can to ensure
that we have the means and the resources to address any emergency. By
allowing for a broader range of vehicles to serve this role, and which
as authorized emergency vehicles could be fitted with lights and sirens
to help navigate through traffic, we will be helping medical transport
teams operate within the sensitive time frames they encounter, which in
turn saves lives.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: A3690A referred to Transportation/S5670 cal. 353

2017-18:  A438A referred to Codes/S2162A passed Senate

2016: A9617A referred to Transportation/S7013 passed Senate

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None to the state.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law. Effective immediately, the addition, amendment
and/or repeal of any rule or regulation necessary for the implementation
of this act on its effective date are authorized and directed to be made
and completed on or before such effective date.

summary: Designates human organ delivery vehicles as authorized emergency vehicles which shall permit the operator of such vehicles certain privileges when involved in an emergency operation.
